subject: ela
cluster: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity
intro: Eleventh graders read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 11-CCR (college and career readiness) complexity band proficiently, applying all skills: multiple central ideas, strong evidence, complex interactions, word meaning, structure, author's purpose and rhetoric, and evaluating reasoning.

items.prompt:
Read.

The revolution in communications connected the world instantly, but it also concentrated power in a few platforms and eroded privacy.

Name TWO central ideas.

steps: One: instant global connection. Two: concentrated power and lost privacy.
So the two central ideas are global connection and its costs (power concentration, lost privacy).
solution.answer: Instant global connection, and its costs (concentrated power, lost privacy).

items.prompt:
Read (same passage).

Name one COST mentioned.

steps: So one cost is eroded privacy.
solution.answer: Eroded privacy (or concentrated power in a few platforms).

items.prompt:
Read.

'We must choose: act now, or explain to our children why we didn't.'

What rhetorical feature drives this line?

steps: It frames the issue as an urgent moral choice and appeals to the future.
So it uses an emotional, future-focused appeal (and a near-ultimatum).
solution.answer: An urgent moral framing and an emotional appeal to the future.

items.prompt:
